{{Short description|Vector space in functional analysis}}
In [[mathematics]], more specifically in [[functional analysis]], a subset <math>T</math> of a [[topological vector space]] <math>X</math> is said to be a '''total''' subset of <math>X</math> if the [[linear span]] of <math>T</math> is a [[Dense set|dense subset]] of <math>X.</math>{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|p=80}} 
This condition arises frequently in many theorems of functional analysis.

== Examples ==

Unbounded [[self-adjoint operator]]s on [[Hilbert space]]s are defined on total subsets.
